Only one measurement exists: the template baseline (acc 0.012, time 0.14 s), which is a demo and tells us nothing about real recipes. All beliefs below are priors, not results.

Mechanisms I believe (unverified here):
1. Epochs-to-target dominates time (H1). An airbench96-style net at about 9 epochs is plausibly near 75% on CIFAR-100, but the published airbench96 figure was for CIFAR-10. The CIFAR-100 75% bar at 9 epochs is aggressive. I expect a first port to land around 0.70-0.75 and probably miss 0.753. Hyperparameters such as lr 9.0 and wd 0.012 are scaled for airbench's loss-sum convention, and a port can easily get this wrong.
2. Systems gains (GPU data, channels_last fp16, compile) are real but usually smaller than hypothesised. Typical gains are 5-15% for compile, and 3% or less for CUDA graphs when the GPU is already saturated at batch 1024. torch.compile with max-autotune may also have a fixed cost that leaks into timed code.
3. Fixed costs (prepare, whitening, data transfer) are probably 0.2-0.5 s, not >10%.
4. Noise: the per-seed accuracy std is about 0.2-0.4 pp, so a 3-seed mean has std of about 0.15-0.25 pp. Run-to-run time noise is about 1-2%. Most small tweaks (EMA, LS 0.3 vs 0.2, alternating flip) have effects of 0.1-0.3 pp, which is comparable to the noise, so they will be inconclusive or null more often than hypothesised. Past gains partly regress, so I shade claimed gains downward.
5. Time is estimated on A100 for roughly 9 epochs of a 128/384/576 net at about 1 s per epoch or less, so about 8-12 s total including overheads.

Unsure: whether the port hits 0.753 at all, the real step time, and Muon's behaviour on CIFAR-100.

forecasts.reason: The first port likely falls a bit below the 0.753 bar at 9 epochs, and mean time is probably near or above 9.5 s.
The slope of about 0.3 pp per half epoch is smaller than the noise, so the measured accuracy change is only weakly informative.
Compile probably saves 5-12%, so the 10% bar is borderline, and max-autotune risks leaking cost into timed code.
The EMA gain is expected to be about 0.1-0.3 pp, which is within noise.
Time should repeat within 2% and the per-seed std should land around 0.2-0.4 pp, as H4.1.1 states.
Savings of 0.3 s are unlikely if the ragged batch was already warmed up in build.
Muon on a port without tuning is unlikely to give 10% fewer epochs, and Newton-Schulz adds overhead.
Progressive resizing at a short schedule usually costs more than 0.2 pp, and the 5% time saving is offset by the accuracy loss.

cruxes: Does the plain airbench96-style port at 9 epochs reach 0.753 on CIFAR-100, or does it need more epochs?
What is the real per-epoch time on the A100 under the 4-CPU pin, and how large is the fixed prepare cost?
What is the per-seed accuracy std, which sets how much margin above 0.753 is needed?
